conviction_note: Mild positive lean: the FQ3 revenue bar (~$16.0-16.3M) sits at the depressed FQ2 run-rate while the Academy load-in that the CEO said slipped from Q2 into Q3 and a $2.3M tariff refund received after May 31 both land in this quarter. But the name has sold its last two full prints by 31-34% on the forward story, DTC is still weak, and the stock ran +15.9% in five sessions into the print. So p_up is only 54 on a 20% absolute move from the rebuilt full-print history, giving +1.6. The findings sum (+2.1) is close to that and is a separate measurement.
bar: FQ3 2026 (quarter ended 2026-08-31) consensus revenue ~$16.0-16.3M and EPS -$0.14 to -$0.16. Earningswhispers has $16.0M / -$0.14 with a whisper of -$0.18 (https://earningswhispers.com/article/BYRN/20303). MarketBeat 2026-10-01 has $16.27M / -$0.1625 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-byrna-technologies-byrn-expected-to-release-earnings-on-thursday-2026-10-01/). StockStory 2026-10-07 has -42.7% YoY on $28.2M, about $16.2M, with estimates 'reconfirmed over the last 30 days' (https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nasdaq/byrn/news/earnings/byrna-byrn-reports-earnings-tomorrow-what-to-expect-2). The three sources agree, so the bar is sourced. The company gave no quantitative guidance, only 'FY2026 will not be a revenue-growth year' and H2 better than H1. FY2026 consensus is $88.1M (3 analysts, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/byrn/forecast/). FQ1 $29.0M plus FQ2 $16.4M is $45.4M, so the implied FQ4 bar is about $26.5M, against $35.2M a year ago (about -25% YoY).

The previous settlements were 1.30M (08-31), 1.54M (08-14), 1.83M (07-31), 2.10M (07-15) and 2.96M (05-29), so shorts covered heavily after the July crash and have only ticked up since (https://equibles.com/stocks/byrn/shortinterest). Tape: spot $3.79, +15.9% over 5 sessions and +5.6% over 20, 86% below the 52-week high and 19% above the low. The 5-day run-up has no identified news cause. Holders: FMR 7.2% (13G/A, event 2026-07-31), Ganz family 9.6% (13D/A 2026-09-08), BlackRock down to 1.7% (13G/A, event 2026-06-30). Turnover is about $1.1M/day.

findings.finding: The Academy Sports + Outdoors initial load-in slipped out of FQ2 and into FQ3 (Jun-Aug). CEO Conn Davis on the 2026-07-09 call: 'that shifted from a load-in from Q2 into Q3, just from a timing end on their side'. Separately, management targets ~200-250 Academy doors by end-2026 after an initial ~50. In FQ2 wholesale was only $5.7M (dealer/chain -47%) against a FQ3 consensus of ~$16.2M, so a pipeline fill of even 50-150 doors ($1-3M) is 6-18% of the quarterly revenue bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue is the line this stock trades on. FQ2 revenue -43% (dealer reorders -47%) drew -33.7% on 2026-07-09. FQ1 dealer revenue +120% (a restocking load-in) was pre-announced on 2026-03-09 (-9.9%), and the full FQ1 print on 2026-04-09 still fell -31.0%: a wholesale load-in has not been rewarded on its own when the outlook disappoints. FQ3 2025, with retail-driven revenue up 35%, drew +21.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: It was said on a public call, so the analysts heard it. But the FQ3 consensus (~$16.2M) is flat to the FQ2 actual ($16.4M) despite summer seasonality, so it is unclear whether the load-in is in the number. If the market had fully priced an Academy fill on top of a flat DTC base, the bar would sit above FQ2 or estimates would have moved up. StockStory says estimates were 'reconfirmed' over 30 days and the whisper (-$0.18) sits below consensus. Net of the rest of the company: DTC (~2/3 of revenue, $11.0M in FQ2) was described as flat into Q3 in a seasonally slow summer, so the load-in partly offsets DTC softness rather than adding cleanly.
findings.independence: Academy.com product pages for the Byrna CL Universal Kit and SD Kinetic Kit exist (https://www.academy.com/p/byrna-cl-universal-kit, page blocked to fetch, so no store-availability data). Investor deck 2026-08-25, slide 14, lists Academy among big-box partners (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1354866/000143774926028928/slide14.jpg). Shares the Q2-call document with the DTC-trends finding.

findings.finding: The FQ2 10-Q says 'Subsequent to May 31, 2026, the Company received an additional tariff refund of approximately $2.3 million'. That cash arrived inside FQ3. In FQ2 the CFO said a $1.1M tariff refund was 'recorded in cost of goods sold', so the same treatment would add about $2.3M (~14 points of gross margin on $16M revenue, ~$0.10/share on 23.4M shares) to GAAP results against an EPS consensus of -$0.14 to -$0.16.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FQ2 carried a $1.1M refund in COGS alongside a $5.9M inventory write-down and a $3.5M impairment; the stock fell -33.7% on revenue, and the refund was invisible in the reaction. There is no instance of this name trading on a below-the-line or one-off item.
findings.why_not_priced: It is in the 10-Q body, not in the press release or the call summaries. Whether the three estimates include it is unknown. If they did, the EPS consensus would sit nearer -$0.05 than -$0.14/-$0.16 on ~$16M revenue at a ~62% underlying margin. A headline GAAP EPS 'beat' is likely, but it is a one-off with no path to guidance, so it is sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: Q2 call transcript (CFO: '$1.1 million tariff refund recorded in cost of goods sold') establishes the accounting treatment: https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/BYRN/Q22026. Same company, different document.

findings.finding: Personal-protection demand was strong during Byrna's FQ3 months. NSSF-adjusted NICS checks were +11.7% YoY in June, +8.5% in July and +2.2% in August 2026, the seventh straight month of gains. Sportsman's Warehouse (a Byrna omni-channel partner) reported Hunting & Shooting Sports +6.7% (firearms +8%, ammo +11%) for May-Jul 2026, 'partially influenced by event-driven demand', and lists personal protection as a core pursuit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no company-level history of the stock trading on industry series. In FQ2 (Mar-May 2026) NICS was +1.6% to +3.2% while Byrna revenue fell 43%, so transmission from this series to Byrna has been weak recently.
findings.why_not_priced: Industry series arrive monthly and nobody maps them to a three-analyst microcap. Had they been priced, FQ3 estimates would have risen from the FQ2 run-rate, and StockStory says they were reconfirmed instead. It is a proxy: management's own statement that e-commerce traffic and conversion were 'fairly consistent' from end-Q2 into Q3 is the more direct read and argues against strong transmission, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: Sportsman's Warehouse Q2 2026 (period ended 2026-08-01), CEO quote on event-driven demand and personal protection: https://sgbonline.com/exec-sportsmans-warehouse-ceo-paul-stone-talks-back-half-plan-healthiest-inventory-in-years/ (2026-09-02); SPWH 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001132105/000119312526378410/spwh-ex99_pr120722.htm

Former CEO Bryan Ganz (IRA, 44,200 sh at ~$3.43) and Mrs. Ganz (8,000 sh at $3.39) bought on 2026-07-17; director Chris Reed bought 8,150 sh at $3.63 on 2026-07-24; director Leonard Elmore bought 10,000 sh at $4.64 on 2026-08-06. findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no measured reaction to insider buying on this name. The Ganz family holds 9.6% (13D/A 2026-09-08).
findings.why_not_priced: The buys are public on Forms 4 and the 13D/A, but they are small and the stock has round-tripped from ~$4.64 to $3.29 and back to $3.79. Buying in the open window right after the FQ2 release is routine, and Elmore's August buy two-thirds into the quarter is the only one with real intra-quarter visibility. Weak signal, sized small.

findings.finding: Similarweb shows byrna.com visits down 16.52% month-over-month in September 2026 (the first month of FQ4), with ~745K visits over the last three months, US rank down 2,430 places. In September 2025 the company reported daily sessions rising from ~50K in August to ~58K in September. That makes a soft start to the holiday quarter, the period management has staked the recovery on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Web traffic and conversion were the cited causes of the FQ2 e-commerce decline (-35%) that drew -33.7%. The Q1 2026 full print fell -31% on a near-term outlook that flagged e-commerce challenges.
findings.why_not_priced: Third-party traffic panels are not in the wire copy, and the implied FQ4 bar (~$26.5M, -25% YoY) has not been cut. If the market had read a weak September, the 5-day run-up of +15.9% would be hard to explain. It is a panel estimate rather than the company's own sessions metric, and a single month, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Earningswhispers preview: byrna.com traffic -13% YoY and conversion 0.59% vs 1.0% (an earlier period, company-reported): https://earningswhispers.com/article/BYRN/20303. Points the same way on DTC weakness.

findings.finding: Management told the market on 2026-07-09 that FQ3 would be weak. CFO: 'Q3 is always a challenge from a seasonality perspective... The summer tends to be the slower months'. CEO: e-commerce traffic and conversion were 'fairly consistent from the end of Q2 into the start of Q3', i.e. still near the FQ2 level where DTC was $11.0M (e-commerce -35% YoY). The new CEO frames FQ3 as 'a transition period' with recovery pushed to the holiday quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last two full prints (2026-04-09 -31.0%, 2026-07-09 -33.7%) both fell hard on DTC weakness and the outlook. StockStory notes 'a history of missing Wall Street revenue projections over the past two years'.
findings.why_not_priced: This is mostly inside what the company already told the market, so it is sized toward 0. The residual risk is that summer seasonality pushes DTC below FQ2's $11.0M, which a consensus flat to FQ2 does not allow for. This is the counterweight to the Academy finding: read together, revenue lands near the bar unless one side is large.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2-call document with the Academy finding. Earningswhispers preview (CEO 'transition period' framing): https://earningswhispers.com/article/BYRN/20303

findings.finding: The holiday-quarter bar is low relative to the retail set-up management described. FY2026 consensus of $88.1M less FQ1 $29.0M, FQ2 $16.4M and FQ3 ~$16.2M implies FQ4 of about $26.5M, against $35.2M a year ago (-25%). Meanwhile management flagged retail holiday load-ins starting late Q3, an Academy target of ~200-250 doors by end-2026, ~1,500 retailer/dealer doors, new SVPs for Retail & Channel Growth (2026-07-20) and Brand & Marketing (2026-08-10), and a new iHeart 'Bobby Bones Show' campaign (2026-09-29).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FQ1 2026 full print fell -31% despite pre-announced revenue of +11%, on near-term outlook commentary. The holiday commentary is where this stock has moved most. A new CEO's first holiday framing can be conservative (kitchen-sink) or a firming, and there is no history under Davis beyond two negative prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The implied Q4 is arithmetic nobody publishes: earningswhispers is still quoting a stale $115M FY number. A -25% YoY holiday bar with retail doors expanding gives management room to firm. But the company has given no numeric guide and marketing spend is ramping (~$250k/month new agency cost plus campaigns), so the sign is uncertain and the size is small.
findings.independence: Q2 call (retail holiday load-ins beginning late Q3, Q4 strongest): https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/BYRN/Q22026. Company news list (SVP hires, Bobby Bones campaign): https://www.stocktitan.net/news/BYRN/

findings.finding: Liquidity is not a near-term overhang. The FQ2 10-Q shows cash of $9.4M ($10.4M with marketable securities), no debt, and an undrawn $5M revolver plus $15M delayed-draw term loan with Texas Capital Bank. Management guided cash 'stable through Q3' and a $5M inventory reduction ($30.4M inventory) feeding Q4 cash, and the $2.3M tariff refund arrived in FQ3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no financing event in the reaction history. No S-3, 424B or ATM filing appears on EDGAR since the FQ2 10-Q (filings list through 2026-09-29).
findings.why_not_priced: On a stock down 86%, a reader may assume a raise is coming. The undrawn $20M facility and no shelf activity make dilution into the print unlikely. If cash fell well below $9M, this flips negative. The money question: the facility is unused, and the refund plus inventory sell-down fund the FQ4 marketing ramp.
findings.independence: EDGAR submissions list shows no S-3/424B/ATM through 2026-09-29: https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001354866.json. Q2 call ('cash to remain stable through Q3'): https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/BYRN/Q22026

findings.finding: The HERO Defense Systems asset acquisition closed in FQ3 (8-K items 2.01 and 3.02 filed 2026-08-10), for $625k cash and $625k in restricted stock plus a royalty. It adds the HERO 2020 argon launcher and the AIIRO gel spray at lower price points, with Byrna.com integration targeted for late Q3/Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-07-08 announcement came the day before the FQ2 print, so its reaction is not separable from the -33.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: Immaterial in dollars and fully public. It matters only if management quantifies HERO's contribution in the Q4 outlook.

findings.finding: No preliminary FQ3 revenue release was issued. Byrna pre-announced its stronger quarters: FQ3 2025 on 2025-09-04, and FQ1 2026 (+11% to $29.0M) on 2026-03-09, days after Davis took over. It did not pre-announce the weak FQ2, and the only 8-Ks since quarter-end are board changes, an investor deck (2026-08-25, no FQ3 data) and annual-meeting results.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pre-announcements moved the stock on their own day (-6.75% on 2025-09-04, -9.9% on 2026-03-09), so the full prints carried less revenue news. This print carries all of it.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an inference from an absence, so per the document-beats-inference rule it is sized near 0. Under the new CEO the habit may simply have changed. Mainly it means the full revenue surprise lands in this print, which raises abs_move.

baseline_tension: The options give no directional statement (unusable chain, no skew). The +15.9% 5-day run-up with no identified cause cuts against a long lean by raising the bar into the print, so p_up is held at 54 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 2 (one-offs): tariff refund cut from +1.0 to +0.5. It has no path to guidance, and the FQ2 refund was invisible in a -33.7% reaction.

Lesson 5 (proxy vs direct): NICS/SPWH proxy cut from +0.8 to +0.4, because management's own statement that DTC trends were flat into Q3 is more direct and FQ2 showed no transmission. Similarweb panel cut from -0.8 to -0.6. Absence-of-prelim inference cut from -0.5 to -0.2.
Lesson 9 (net of the rest): Academy load-in cut from +1.5 to +1.2, net of DTC (~2/3 of revenue) seasonally softer than FQ2.
Positioning/insider weak-signal check: insider buying cut from +0.5 to +0.4, since open-window buying after a release is routine.
Untrustworthy history rule: abs_move rebuilt from confirmed full prints only (-33.7, -31.0, +11.6, +21.2, -21.3; median |21.3|), so abs_move was raised from 15 to 20.
Lesson 1 (reaction function): the last two full prints sold off 31-34% on outlook, so p_up was moved from 55 to 54. The scaled number moves from +1.5 to +1.6 only because abs_move rose.
